Not listed in the official requirements.
Cambridge asks for transcripts and certificates for each degree you have taken. PDF under 2MB, not encrypted; non-English documents need a registered translator's full translation.
Official transcripts for each degree. If still studying, an interim or unofficial transcript is fine; you will need the final one if you get an offer. PDF under 2MB.
A CV uploaded through the Cambridge Applicant Portal.
Two academic references for Cambridge admission plus one separate Gates Cambridge reference that ranks you against the scholarship criteria. Referees submit online by the deadline.
Cambridge lists a personal statement as a standard document; check your course page. The four Gates selection questions (200-300 words each) are answered in the online form.
PhD applicants only. Usually uploaded with your Cambridge documents; if not, you must submit it for the Gates Cambridge application. Use a separate tailored proposal for each course.
Gates Cambridge does not require a research proposal for non-PhD degrees. Your course page may ask for one.
Only if English is not your first language. For most courses it is needed only once you hold an offer. Gates Cambridge itself sets no English test requirement.
GRE only if your course page asks for it; GMAT is not accepted.
Written work only if your course asks for it.
